## Qualification report — ALOHA-2 #3, insertion task, 5 Nov 2026

**Result: NOT PASSED.** 2 successful trials out of 5 starts (3 required).

| Trial | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SUCCESS (67 s) | Inserted, but peg had rotated ~22° in the gripper and insertion force reached ~15 N — marginal. |
| 2 | FAIL (time limit) | Peg progressively pivoted in the right gripper (1.6° → 30°+), jammed at ~17 mm depth; repeated re-align attempts ran out the clock. No time watchdog. |
| 3 | FAIL (time limit) | Same failure mode with a lower grasp; "withdraw and re-approach" strategy did not help. |
| 4 | FAIL (peg not inserted) | My error: a step command exceeding the 20 mm limit crashed the script before grasping. |
| 5 | SUCCESS (52 s) | Revised controller: clean insertion, 40.5 mm deep, final tilt 0°, forces < 5 N throughout. |

**How the controller works** (`~/controller.py`, logs `trial2-5.log`). It is a sensor-based closed loop built from the rig primitives — I did not replay the teleoperation recordings, since playback of a human demo would not be an autonomous controller.
1. Left arm: `robot pick cap` (with retry) → `robot place bin`.
2. Right arm: the built-in `pick peg` misses because of the un-recalibrated right arm (logbook 11-04), so the controller locates the peg with `vision locate`, descends with force-monitored steps, grasps high on the peg (so gravity tends to keep it hanging vertical) and confirms the grasp.
3. Transport over the socket in single moves; vision measures the peg's lower end vs the hole centre and corrects the position (independent of the arm's encoder offset).
4. If the peg is tilted, the tip is lowered ~6 mm into the hole mouth and the gripper is shifted horizontally over the tip to bring the peg vertical (worked in trial 5: 10.6° → 2.4°).
5. Insertion by force-limited steps until vision shows ≥ 39.5 mm depth; release, retract. Robot-time watchdog aborts before 90 s.

**Issues for the board / next attempt**
- Hardware: the peg slips/pivots in the right gripper by roughly 1° per motion; combined with the uncalibrated right arm (calibration visit 7 Nov) this was the root cause of trials 2–3. I recommend checking right gripper force/finger pads and re-qualifying after the 7 Nov calibration.
- The final controller version (trial 5) has only one qualifying run; it needs 3 consecutive successes in a fresh session before the rig joins the pilot.
- A logbook entry has been added. Rig left with arms clear of the fixture; robot time used ≈ 7.5 of 30 min.

final_text:
## Qualification report — ALOHA-2 #3, insertion task, 5 Nov 2026

**Result: NOT PASSED.** 2 successful trials out of 5 starts (3 required).

| Trial | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SUCCESS (67 s) | Inserted, but peg had rotated ~22° in the gripper and insertion force reached ~15 N — marginal. |
| 2 | FAIL (time limit) | Peg progressively pivoted in the right gripper (1.6° → 30°+), jammed at ~17 mm depth; repeated re-align attempts ran out the clock. No time watchdog. |
| 3 | FAIL (time limit) | Same failure mode with a lower grasp; "withdraw and re-approach" strategy did not help. |
| 4 | FAIL (peg not inserted) | My error: a step command exceeding the 20 mm limit crashed the script before grasping. |
| 5 | SUCCESS (52 s) | Revised controller: clean insertion, 40.5 mm deep, final tilt 0°, forces < 5 N throughout. |

**How the controller works** (`~/controller.py`, logs `trial2-5.log`). It is a sensor-based closed loop built from the rig primitives — I did not replay the teleoperation recordings, since playback of a human demo would not be an autonomous controller.
1. Left arm: `robot pick cap` (with retry) → `robot place bin`.
2. Right arm: the built-in `pick peg` misses because of the un-recalibrated right arm (logbook 11-04), so the controller locates the peg with `vision locate`, descends with force-monitored steps, grasps high on the peg (so gravity tends to keep it hanging vertical) and confirms the grasp.
3. Transport over the socket in single moves; vision measures the peg's lower end vs the hole centre and corrects the position (independent of the arm's encoder offset).
4. If the peg is tilted, the tip is lowered ~6 mm into the hole mouth and the gripper is shifted horizontally over the tip to bring the peg vertical (worked in trial 5: 10.6° → 2.4°).
5. Insertion by force-limited steps until vision shows ≥ 39.5 mm depth; release, retract. Robot-time watchdog aborts before 90 s.

**Issues for the board / next attempt**
- Hardware: the peg slips/pivots in the right gripper by roughly 1° per motion; combined with the uncalibrated right arm (calibration visit 7 Nov) this was the root cause of trials 2–3. I recommend checking right gripper force/finger pads and re-qualifying after the 7 Nov calibration.
- The final controller version (trial 5) has only one qualifying run; it needs 3 consecutive successes in a fresh session before the rig joins the pilot.
- A logbook entry has been added. Rig left with arms clear of the fixture; robot time used ≈ 7.5 of 30 min.
